answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, and the deposit grows with the work it claims, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits. A lightweight monitor, a sparrow watching from its knoll, flags clusters whose attestations move in lockstep. When fraud is proven the bond is slashed, and the delta between honest earnings and attack cost turns negative, so faking identities loses money instead of making it.
